problem: Given that $u=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]$ is a non-zero  vector that is orthogonal to the set $W={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]},$ find the value of $\frac{c}{a+b}.$
worked_solution:
The vector $u$ is orthogonal to the set $W$ if $u\cdot {w}_{1}=0$ and $u\cdot {w}_{2}=0.$ So, we need to solve the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}u\cdot {w}_{1}=0 \\ u\cdot {w}_{2}=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M,$ which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 10 & -5 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, we have $2$ pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd), so ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}{x}_{3}.$ So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{x}_{3} \\ \frac{1}{2}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{3}=2,$ we get the vector 
$[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, we obtain $a=1,$ $b=1,$ and $c=2.$

Finally, $\frac{c}{a+b}=\frac{2}{1+1}=1.$
